order: This change builds the dispatch layer over the existing registry. It ships as a router module at the repository root, and the plan's casting tables become a single data file listing the rungs, the roles, the review matrix, the ladder, and the trigger rules, so the router reads them instead of hardcoding anything. Every rung then gets checked against an independent transcription of the source table in both directions before it ships. The route function fails closed on any ownership-invariant violation, resolving a role only through a registry that loads clean. Reviewer selection computes no-self-family status from the full co-author set, so unattributed or mixed-family authorship fails closed rather than dispatching open. A missing required companion task blocks the dispatch entirely, and any default the plan leaves silent gets marked as an explicit unstated choice, while the gate order, cross-vendor review before code ships, stays just as it was.
claims: 74 checks went green, and an exhaustive sweep across every bucket-state combination confirmed that no mandatory-class dispatch ever produces a same-family closing verdict. No-self-family behavior was checked for every author-family combination in turn, and an independent bidirectional transcription check confirmed that every rung matches the source table exactly. Fail-closed loading was then tamper-tested against registry corruption, never-rule violations, vendor and family mismatches, and off-ladder inputs, so the pipeline now runs the full suite on every change.
